clue.text: Part of calm, atypical Asian capital

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is wanted, a run of consecutive letters lifted from inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of calm and the start of atypical

explanation.surface: A traveller finds part of some Asian capital unusually calm.
explanation.walkthrough: Almaty, in Kazakhstan, was the country's capital until 1997 and is still its largest city.
explanation.definitionFit: Almaty is a former national capital in Central Asia, so it is an example of an Asian capital city.

clue.text: Saw pair mosh wildly

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone watched a couple dancing wildly in a mosh pit at a gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' reads as the past tense of see; here it is the noun meaning an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional proverb or maxim, and an aphorism is a pithy statement of a general truth, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Thinking of people heading out of Waterloo?

parts.note: men are people

explanation.surface: A thought about crowds of commuters pouring out of Waterloo station.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo is one of London's main railway terminals; the question mark flags that it stands for the general word, with its first letter dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Mentation is a formal word for mental activity or the process of thought, so it is a synonym of thinking.

clue.text: US theatre awards excluding new plays

parts.note: the Tony Awards honour Broadway theatre

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plays' looks like a noun about theatre, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with something is to play with it idly, so toys and plays are synonymous verbs.

clue.text: Most negligible, almost negative tax

explanation.surface: A tax that is barely negative counts as the most negligible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax' suggests money, but here it is the verb meaning to put under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutest is the superlative of minute, meaning tiniest, so it describes the least significant or most negligible amount.

clue.text: One's turned white, transfixed

parts.note: one is I, and I's means I am, written I'M
to pale is to turn white

explanation.surface: Someone admits turning pale with shock, frozen to the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transfixed' suggests being spellbound, but the answer takes its literal sense of being pierced through.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfix literally means to pierce through with a sharp object, which is exactly what impaled means.

clue.text: Point circled by cycling duo, old and cross

definitions.text: Point circled by cycling duo, old and cross

indicators.text: Point circled by cycling duo, old and cross
indicators.note: the clue has no separate definition: being itself so irregular, the whole sentence stands for its answer
letters cycling round move their front one to the back, so the word after it is rotated
something circled by another thing has that thing all around it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: duo with its first letter moved to the end
north is a point of the compass
O is the abbreviation for old
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: A grumpy old pair cycles round a point.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word is wordplay, leaving no definition; the blogger reads the whole clue as self-describing, an irregular clue for its own answer. A later online version added 'eccentric' as a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue lacking any definition breaks convention, so the clue itself is an example of something irregular and unconventional.

clue.text: Leaves chaps in Barking
